_comment: Portes du Soleil. Audit sign-offs, plus one hand-elevation patch at Avoriaz. See src/config/resorts.ts for the Roc d'Enfer exclusion box.
_comment_setNodeElevation: AVORIAZ VILLAGE PATCH â€” the case where BOTH sources are wrong, which is exactly what setNodeElevation is for. Our elevation provider reads this shelf 5-76 m TOO LOW, and the second DEM (Terrarium) reads it 3-7 m TOO HIGH, almost certainly sampling the tops of Avoriaz's tall timber-clad apartment blocks rather than the snow. Because neither source is competent here, the elevation-consensus pass DECLINES the whole 22-node patch (that is the atomic-patch guard working as designed â€” half a repair drops a step into the middle of the fault) and it can only be resolved by hand. Every value below was read off the contours on the debug map by the user, not derived. The load-bearing facts: the three lift bottoms Stade / Lac-Intrets / Tour are LEVEL with each other at ~1737 m (our data spread them over 17 m and put Tour 11 m too HIGH, which is why the links between them came out one-way instead of bidirectional), and Surf sits ~8 m above them at ~1745 m. DO NOT replace these with a DEM sample on the next refresh, and do not widen any tolerance to make the automatic pass accept this patch â€” it is right to refuse it.

setNodeElevation._why: Stade Tete au Boeuf (bottom) â€” the node the FIRST pass of this patch missed, and the proof that a half-patched fault is worse than an unpatched one: pinning the four lift bases around it left this one 17-25 m below them, every run bottomed out here, and it became a 22-node trapped basin that did not exist before. Read off the contours by the user like the rest.
Synthetic snap copies sit at their parent node's height â€” confirmed by the user's own readings for sn362907957 and sn7021400781, which both matched their parent exactly.

The same sunken shelf continues a few metres east — Retour Chavanette's bottom and the node beside Stade. Read off the contours by the user at ~1737-1738 m, i.e. level with the lift bases 27 m away, not 9-17 m below them.

Lift top station. The OSM point sits at ~1750 m where the cable enters the building; the skier exit is at ~1760 m, which is the elevation that matters for routing (this is the station the runs must leave FROM).

Prodains Express 3S top: the forecourt 11 m NE of the station, where the Crot and Bleue d'Arare stubs meet the arrival. Read off the contours as level with the station deck (1760). Our provider had it at 1737 and the second DEM agrees with 1751, but both are reading the ground beside the raised arrival platform, not the deck a skier stands on. Left uncorrected it was a DEAD END - six edges in, zero out - so every short run off the gondola top ended there and a skier was stuck.

Prodains Express 3S top: the Crot junction on the same arrival flat, 75 m SE of the station. Read as level with the deck (1760); our provider had 1765 and the second DEM 1759. This is what makes the Crot stub e2183 and the station link e4941 two-way, which is how the arrival actually skis - you can drift either way across the flat.

Prodains Express 3S top: the Bleue d'Arare stub end on the same arrival flat, 24 m N of the station. Level with the deck (1760). Left alone the elevation-consensus pass drove it DOWN to 1752 and the 21 m stub read as a 39% pitch.

Fornet chairlift TOP station, above Avoriaz on the Hauts Forts side. User read 2211 m off the contours - level with the Fornet junction n270740419 87 m SW, not 18 m below it. Both DEMs sample 2192/2193 here because they hit the ground beside the raised arrival deck, the same error as the Prodains 3S top. This was the resort's ONLY reversal candidate: at 2193 the only way in to n270740419 was an 18 m lift-access climb, which is exactly the shape check:elevation flags as a suspect elevation. At 2211 the 120 m Fornet link between them is level and two-way, and the flag goes away on its own.
Stade â€” bottom station, level with Lac-Intrets and Tour.
Lac-Intrets â€” bottom station, level with Stade and Tour.
Tour â€” bottom station. The only node in the patch our data placed too HIGH (1748 vs ~1737), which is why it never looked like part of the same sunken fault.
Surf â€” bottom station, ~8 m ABOVE the other three, not level with them.

acceptedDeadEnds.why: Top of runs '54' (blue) and '56' (red), Braitaz sector â€” OPEN OSM GAP, signed off pending an upstream fix, NOT a defect on our side. n13289373141 @1626 m has no in-edges at all; n13289373143 @1609 m is flagged only because its sole feed is that orphan. Below them everything drains normally (54 -> n281370219 @1570, 56 -> n7366125507 @1509). Verified: OSM w1448462122 ('54', easy) starts EXACTLY at n13289373141 (vertex 0, 0 m), so we imported it complete; elevations are sound (second DEM agrees within 1-5 m: 1626/1609/1570); there is NO abandoned:/disused: lift anywhere in the box, so unlike Torgon nothing was dismantled; and there is no other piste within 600 m of the top, nor any node higher than 1626 m within 988 m. The nearest lift, the Panthiaz gondola, tops out 348 m away and 139 m BELOW. The piste map has 54 served by TÃ©lÃ©siÃ¨ge de Braitaz, whose top station (1799 m) in OSM only feeds the red 'Blanchot', landing 988 m away. CONCLUSION: OSM is missing the run â€” most likely a blue â€” that brings you from the Braitaz/Blanchot side across to the top of 54. Reviewed on the map by the user, who reached the same conclusion: real terrain, real missing feed, but we do not have the information to draw it. REJECTED ALTERNATIVES: (a) reversing the arrows so you enter 54 from the green below and climb to the top of 56 â€” that is 39 m of ascent over 425 m with the final pitches at 8% and 15%, far beyond maxTraverseClimb (8 m) and flatGradeMax (6%), and not a momentum traverse; (b) deleting the 145 m stub above the junction â€” it is part of OSM way 54 itself, so removing it just moves the orphan down to n13289373143. DO NOT invent a connector here. RE-CHECK ON REFRESH: if OSM gains the missing run these nodes stop being trapped and check:trapped will report this entry as stale â€” that WARN is the signal to come back and delete this sign-off.

Torgon / La Jorette (Swiss side) â€” the 2.1 km blue chain descending from 1621 m through 1503 / 1341 / 1329 / 1181 m to the two dead ends at 1142 and 1143 m in the Vionnaz valley. Reported as 5 trapped + 3 orphan nodes, but it is ONE connected descent, not eight defects. THE LIFTS THAT SERVED IT HAVE BEEN DISMANTLED, and OSM says so explicitly: w44538226 'TÃ©lÃ©siÃ¨ge Jorette' is abandoned:aerialway=chair_lift, w45666705 'TÃ©lÃ©siÃ¨ge Grands Places' is abandoned:aerialway=chair_lift, and w44538224 'Fignards' is disused:aerialway=drag_lift. Their positions land on the stranded chain itself â€” Jorette's centre (46.30924,6.86262) sits on n565736424 @1341 / n14050186237 @1329, and Fignards' centre (46.31198,6.86650) sits on n14050186233 @1181, the node feeding both bottom dead ends. Corroborated off-map: the chairlifts linking Torgon La Jorette to the main Plan-de-Croix area were decommissioned and the link is now shuttle bus only; just beginner lifts remain at La Jorette. So the pipeline is behaving correctly on every count â€” it imports the pistes (they are still drawn, and still skiable downhill) and refuses the abandoned/disused lifts. NEVER bridge this: any connector added here would fabricate a lift that no longer exists in the real world. Signed off by the user after review.
